groups.why: This verse has no new speaker and carries on Moses's closing words, which the Berean quotation runs on into. Its clauses are parts of that turn.

cant_tell.why: It follows Moses's prayer in Exo.8.5 (cl2), but no command lies between them in this speech, and a result link would reach back across verses without one. Left unlinked.

referents.why: 'he had appointed for Pharaoh' is a masculine singular whose sense is the LORD, who sent the frogs. Aaron stretched out the hand, but the sending is the LORD's; the verb's subject is the LORD.
referents.category: subject of an earlier act by God

links.why: the qatal 'which he had appointed for Pharaoh' is a relative clause inside the noun phrase 'the frogs', the object of cl1's 'on the matter of'.
links.category: relative clause inside a noun phrase

links.why: cl0 (they went out from Pharaoh) is the earlier event and cl1 (Moses cried out) the later. The and-then link runs backward.
a wayyiqtol continues the narrative line; cl0 comes first and cl1 follows.

cant_tell.what: Whether Moses's crying out (cl1) fulfils Pharaoh's command 'pray to the LORD' (Exo.8.4 cl2)
cant_tell.why: fulfils needs a report that the command was carried out, in the did-so form after the command. The text says only that Moses cried out to the LORD, so no link is forced.

links.why: the clauses run cl0, then cl1 (the frogs died). This link reverses that order.
the death of the frogs is what the LORD's act brings about, a result rather than a plain and-then (R4). Replaced by the result link below.
'the LORD did as Moses requested' is the act; the frogs dying is the outcome that follows from it.

cant_tell.what: Whether 'the LORD did as Moses requested' (cl0) is a fulfilment of Moses's request
cant_tell.why: The subject is named, the did-so pro-form (ken) is absent, and the request is a prayer rather than an imperative. fulfils is not forced; it is read as result instead.

referents.why: 'them' is masculine plural. The object is the dead frogs of the previous verse, which are feminine and are not in this verse's candidate list, so no candidate fits.
referents.category: object not among the candidates

referents.why: 'they piled them' is an impersonal third plural. The text does not name who heaped the frogs, and no candidate is the people of Egypt.

links.why: cl0 is the first clause of the verse, so the and-then link runs backward.
the land stinking follows from the heaping of the dead frogs, a state that the act brings about (R4), not a plain and-then. Replaced by the result link below.
the heaping of the dead frogs brings about the stench in the land, the state that follows the act.

cant_tell.what: Who piled the frogs (cl0s) and what 'them' (w3) is
cant_tell.why: The frogs are not a candidate in this verse, and the masculine 'them' does not agree with the feminine frogs. The text gives no other referent.

links.why: 'saw that there was relief': cl1 is what Pharaoh saw, the object of the seeing.

links.why: ka'asher with a qatal saying: the refusal is just as the LORD had said, so the action is declared the fulfilment of an earlier word.

a separate waw on the infinitive absolute: the hardening follows the seeing. The sense does not make the seeing a cause, so it stays a plain and.
a hardened will and then the refusal that follows is the R4 example of a result, not a plain and.
